subject: Rapid fallback strategy + temporary SLA policy exception request
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rapid fallback strategy + temporary SLA policy exception request

Morning team —

Quick context: Acme AI is on a tight launch cadence and flagged a potential spike in inference latency this week during a staged traffic ramp. Their Dedicated cluster is configured with a canary rollout for model v4.2 -> v4.3, and early telemetry shows p95 latency creeping toward our SLA threshold. If this trend continues we risk an SLA trigger and credit exposure.

Request: Can we approve a short-term exception to allow automated rollback/pinning behavior to be elevated for this customer for the next 72 hours? Specifically:
- Allow the serving runtime to automatically revert traffic to the previously pinned model (v4.2) if p95 latency > 220ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows or error rate > 0.8% for any 5-minute window.
- Allow pinning of v4.2 at the routing layer without manual exec sign-off for Dedicated customers on an emergency path.

Why this matters: Manual approvals add an avg 30–60 minute delay; automated fallback reduces blast radius, limits credit exposure, and keeps downstream apps stable. We still want full postmortem and playbook review after the window.

I'd like to capture a short sign-off here from Reliability and Product; Ben, can you confirm this is acceptable from a customer-communication standpoint? Monica, can you flag any technical gaps (canary rules, metric deltas, rollback latency) that would block this? Laura, would you authorize a temporary policy carveout if both teams sign off?

Attaching a draft rollback playbook and a snapshot of the canary metrics we captured this morning.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: rollback_playbook_v3.pdf (playbook), canary-metrics-sla.csv (metrics snapshot)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid fallback strategy + temporary SLA policy exception request

Dylan — thanks for the heads up and the docs. I reviewed the snapshot and the draft playbook. High-level notes:

- Metrics & thresholds: the proposed p95 threshold (220ms) and error rate cutoff (0.8%) are reasonable as short-term tripping conditions. Recommend we use two consecutive 5-minute windows for p95 and a single 1-minute spike detection for error rate to avoid noisy false positives.
- Canary sizing: ensure canary is limited to <= 10% of global traffic and routed by user cohort where possible; noisy cohorts should be excluded from auto-revert.
- Rollback mechanics: automatic fallback will pin the prior model at the routing layer and trigger a circuit-breaker that drains pending requests to the older variant. Estimated mean time to full traffic revert: 45–120s depending on active sessions and KV cache warmup.
- Observability: require an automatic pager (PagerDuty playbook) if auto-revert occurs; include the correlation id (request.batch_id) in the alert payload.

Blocking items before I can greenlight the runtime change (but still OK for exec exception):
1) Confirm that Dedicated cluster RBAC allows temporary pin-by-policy for customer-specific routing (security ops check).
2) Add a canary backoff policy for token-heavy requests to prevent token-burst-induced latency.

If security ops signs off on RBAC and we add the backoff rule, I'm comfortable with Monica-level technical approval for a 72-hour emergency exception.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference

Dylan / Monica — I looped in Sam (customer) to keep them in the loop; they asked for transparency on what "automatic" means and customer-visible behavior. Quick notes for external comms:

- Customer impact: if auto-revert fires, calls will continue to succeed against v4.2; there is no downtime expected. The only customer-observable change is latency improvement and a note in the app logs referencing the revert event.
- Billing/SLA: we should clearly state we will treat any auto-revert as an operational mitigation and not an admission of bug in the model. If the revert prevents an SLA breach, no credit should be issued for that interval; foundation legal has okayed this language in past carveouts but we should confirm for Dedicated contracts.
- Customer consent: Sam asked that we notify them immediately via their SRE channel and share a timeline for post-revert analysis.

I think this is reasonable as a temporary exception provided Reliability and Product sign off on the technical thresholds and Security confirms RBAC. I can patch the external-facing note once Laura signs off on the policy change.

—Ben

Thanks all — I reviewed the thread and attachments. I authorize a time-limited policy exception for Acme AI's Dedicated cluster with the following conditions:

1) Scope & duration: 72-hour window starting when Security posts a config change to the Dedicated routing policy (ETA: within 2 hours of their sign-off).
2) Triggers: auto-revert allowed when either:
   - p95 latency > 220ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows; or
   - error rate > 0.8% for any 1-minute window.
3) Safety controls required before activation:
   - Security Ops must confirm RBAC changes and provide an audit log stream to the customer's compliance mailbox.
   - SRE must attach PagerDuty runbook and ensure the revert alert includes batch_id and canary cohort id.
   - Customer opt-in confirmation (Sam) must be logged in the ticket.
4) Communication & billing: Ben to notify Acme SRE Slack and legal to confirm credit policy wording.
5) Postmortem: A joint postmortem with Acme and internal stakeholders within 5 business days; include latency traces, KV cache warmup timing, and rollout event timeline.

I appreciate the rapid coordination. Please mark the Jira SRE-1129 as blocked->in-progress once Security confirms RBAC.

Laura Bennett
Chief Product Officer, Redwood Inference
